newsitem.title: EGYPT: Mideast water centre set for signing next month.
newsitem.headline: Mideast water centre set for signing next month.

text.p: An agreement establishing a research centre on the desalination of water in the Middle East will be signed next month in the Omani capital of Muscat, the centre's director said on Tuesday.

Eric Jankel said the Middle East Desalination Centre, one of many projects spawned by the Middle East peace process, had financial support from the United States, Israel, Oman, Japan and South Korea. The European Union had promised to provide funding.

"Because we're a byproduct of the peace process we hope to bring people together and find solutions to problems," Jankel told a session on water management at the Middle East/North Africa Economic Conference in Cairo.
Water is not only a scarce resource in the Middle East but also a bitter point of contention between Israelis and Palestinians as well as between other states in the region.
"The object of the research centre is to achieve practical results: to reduce the cost of a cubic metre of water," said Jankel.
He had no figures on how many people the centre would employ or what its annual budget would be. The signing date would be between December 15-20, he added.
